checks.finding: The 2026-08-27 amendment leaves requirements.md self-contradictory and its new exception's predicate undefined. (a) CONTRADICTION: requirements.md:384 now says Resolver Evidence is 'written on every Block, with **three** named exceptions', the third of which (:389-397) writes no Evidence at all; but REQ-004:564-568 still says Evidence is written on every invocation 'with the **sole** exception of a Block reached because Resolver Evidence itself fails its own schema self-validation ... that one case writes nothing at all'. Both are frozen normative statements about the same observable. Before the amendment :565 was accurate (disabled-legacy-invocation still writes a minimal record, so B3 was genuinely the only write-nothing case); the amendment added a second write-nothing case and did not update the sibling. An implementer/test author cannot decide whether an absent resolver-evidence.yaml in the uncontained-staging case is conformant (REQ-002) or a defect (REQ-004), and AC-012 vs AC-020 inherit the same fork. (b) UNDEFINED PREDICATE: the term 'fixed publication write set' occurs only at :390-391 and :395 and is defined nowhere. REQ-002:395 points at 'the fixed write set immediately below', but nothing below in REQ-002 states one (:398-406 is the check-component-coverage mirror and the diagnostic-line format); AC-012:833 instead points at 'REQ-001's fixed write set', and REQ-001 step (m):317-321 defines only a 'track-exclusive output set' {facet-manifest.yaml, project-context.resolved.json, resolver-evidence.yaml} / {capability-summary.yaml, resolver-evidence.yaml}. The two candidate sets in the document yield opposite results: under Security Boundaries:1153-1158 the boundary explicitly INCLUDES 'its own transient specs/<feature>/.resolver-staging/ ... area', so the staging area is never outside it and the exception can never fire; under REQ-001's track-exclusive output set the staging area is always outside it and the exception always fires. Neither reading yields the evidently-intended path-escape semantics. (c) UNREACHABLE/UNENUMERATED TRIGGER: the exception is attached to publication-journal-recovery, whose own row :356 admits exactly two trigger conditions, both journal-convergence failures ('a referenced pre-image backup file is itself missing/unreadable, or a target's current live hash matches neither its journal-recorded PRE nor POST value'), gated on first 'find[ing] a stale transaction journal'. A staging-area containment failure is neither. REQ-001 step (0):255-260 describes only journal convergence and states no containment check, no ordering position for one, and no id for its failure. Consequently, when the staging area is uncontained but no stale journal exists, no row's trigger matches at all — inside a taxonomy REQ-002:349-351 declares 'closed at sixteen rows' with 'no fail-open path exists anywhere in this list'. Downstream: the Phase-2 implementer cannot determine whether to implement the containment check, when it runs, or which id it emits; the fixture author cannot construct the case. This is a Phase-1 defect because both statements are internal to requirements.md's own frozen requirement prose and its own closed enumeration — no design, task, or gate artifact can resolve a contradiction between two requirement sentences. Critical per the calibration's 'contradictory ... impossible acceptance criteria' class and my role's contradiction rule.

Every stated goal REQ-001..REQ-008 carries at least one matching acceptance criterion in requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria table (:820-877): REQ-001 → AC-001..AC-009/AC-038/AC-043/AC-052/AC-054; REQ-002 → AC-010..AC-015/AC-038..AC-041/AC-047..AC-049/AC-055; REQ-003 → AC-015/AC-016/AC-042; REQ-004 → AC-017..AC-021/AC-044/AC-050/AC-051/AC-054/AC-056; REQ-005 → AC-022..AC-025/AC-045; REQ-006 → AC-026..AC-028/AC-045; REQ-007 → AC-029..AC-032/AC-042/AC-046/AC-053; REQ-008 → AC-033/AC-034. The three Global rows AC-035/036/037 are goal-independent registration checks and are documented as such. Caveat recorded under AC-OBSERVABLE rather than failed here: REQ-002's two 2026-08-26 sub-triggers cite AC-057/AC-058, which exist only in acceptance-tests.md; because those two obligations do carry observable test rows within the package, goal-level traceability itself is intact.

Two acceptance-artifact integrity defects, one introduced by the amendment and one left un-propagated by its predecessor. (a) NO TEST TARGET OWNS THE NEW OBLIGATION. acceptance-tests.md AC-012/TEST-012 (:54) excludes 'the uncontained-staging-area sub-case of publication-journal-recovery' and asserts in passing that 'its fixture asserts the canonical diagnostic line is emitted and that no Resolver Evidence and no other live artifact is written' — but no row anywhere in the file creates that fixture. TEST-010 (:52) is a closed enumeration of exactly sixteen fixtures, one per diagnostic id, so it supplies a single publication-journal-recovery fixture; TEST-047 (:86) supplies the crash-between-renames convergence fixture and the corrupted-pre-image companion, neither of which is the staging-containment case. The package's own precedent for a diagnostic id with two distinct sub-cases is a dedicated dual-fixture row — AC-055/TEST-055 (:94) was created for exactly that reason for output-schema-validation-failed — and no equivalent was created here. Combined with the REQ-TESTABILITY(b)/(c) finding, the entry condition is also unstatable, so the obligation is presently neither owned by a test target nor constructible. (b) TWO TEST ROWS HAVE NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IN requirements.md. acceptance-tests.md:97-98 carries AC-057/TEST-057 and AC-058/TEST-058, and requirements.md REQ-002 cites both as governing ('AC-058' at :364, 'AC-057' at :368), but requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria table ends at AC-056 (:877) — grep confirms AC-057/AC-058 appear in requirements.md only inside those two REQ-002 table cells. This contradicts acceptance-tests.md's own stated contract in its preamble: ':3-6 declares TEST IDs 'map 1:1 to requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria by matching row number (AC-NNN ↔ TEST-NNN), with one documented class of exception', and :8-18 documents that single class as AC-035/036/037 (criteria with no TEST row) — the inverse case now present is undocumented; and :29-30 still asserts 'AC-038 through AC-056 are new rows this revision adds', an inventory sentence the 2026-08-26 follow-up left stale. investigation.md:1325 confirms the follow-up added AC-057/AC-058 to acceptance-tests.md and to traceability.md but records no corresponding addition to requirements.md's criterion table. The two rows also sit after a blank line with no table header (:96-98), so as Markdown they are not part of the table at all. Downstream: a task author or verifier deriving the criterion matrix from requirements.md — the document that owns the AC table and whose bytes the review pins — never sees AC-057/AC-058, so REQ-002's two amended sub-triggers (the step-(e) Registry recheck and the absent-component fail-closed rule) carry no criterion in that matrix. Major: downstream mismatch, not a blocking impossibility.

Non-goals (:741-793) explicitly exclude the nine surfaces where this feature could otherwise expand: building the scripts themselves, editing any Epic A1/A2/A3/A4 contract file, adding the required_lite_checks source field to A2's schema, reimplementing check-component-coverage's Fail conditions, owning compare-facet-manifest-staleness's caller, computing decision-v2 §10's full effective enforcement, editing anything under plugins/**, authoring an ADR, and authoring tasks.md/traceability.md. Each is reinforced elsewhere with a named owner: the A2 schema revision is assigned to Epic A2's maintainers with scope and migration (:140-163), the staleness caller to a future epic (:212-217), and the SKILL.md edit to a future implementation task (:780-785, :962-967) with AC-032/TEST-032 locking the commit-scope boundary. The amendment did not disturb these. Non-goals sufficient for this gate.

The approval boundary for the amendment under review is asserted but unrecorded. Four locations now claim human authority for a normative change to a frozen, hash-pinned document — requirements.md:391-392 ('amended 2026-08-27, human-approved, ruling option 4'), requirements.md AC-012:833 (same phrase), and acceptance-tests.md AC-012 (:54) and AC-047 (:86) ('wording aligned 2026-08-27, human-approved, ruling option 4') — but investigation.md's '## Amendment Re-Review Context' section (:792 onward) contains no entry for it: grep over investigation.md returns zero occurrences of '2026-08-27' and zero of 'option 4'. The section records only rulings A(1)/B(1) (2026-08-24, :800-887) and rulings C(1)/C(2) (2026-08-26, :1214-1333). For this amendment there is therefore no full amendment commit hash, no per-document SHA-256 at the amendment commit, and no verbatim dated quotation of the human's approval — the three elements the calibration's :84-96 evidence bar requires, which it also identifies as the only thing that makes an in-conversation approval a durable, citable record. The package's own convention makes the omission conspicuous: the immediately preceding amendment's rows carry explicit pointers ('approval evidence: investigation.md `## Amendment Re-Review Context` › `### Rulings C(1)/C(2)`', requirements.md:364 and :368), and rulings C(1)/C(2) supply the verbatim dated quotation (:1241-1249), amendment commit hashes (:1266-1284), and per-document SHA-256 pins (:1286-1292). The 2026-08-27 rows supply none of these — they are the 'unqualified assertion' the calibration's NOT-suppressed example (:128-132) names. Consequence per the calibration: the amendment re-review declaration does not extend to this amendment, so its later-phase references gain no benefit of the doubt; I have not escalated this to a blanket phase-sequencing finding, because the section does meet the bar for the earlier amendments from which most later-phase references descend. Scoped to spec review because the approval record for a Phase-1 frozen-document amendment is a Phase-1 artifact, and no later gate re-derives it. Remedy is additive and does not touch the amended prose: append a '### Ruling option 4 (human-approved 2026-08-27)' entry with the commit hash, per-document SHA-256 pins, and the verbatim dated approval, and add the pointer to the four citing locations.

Each of the five Risks (:1261-1355) names a concrete validation surface: the required-enforcement Lite block (INV-019/B5) is validated by AC-009/TEST-009's three-non-Blocking-state matrix plus AC-010/TEST-010's required-missing fixture, with the fixturability limit stated honestly (acceptance-tests.md:51 records required-present-empty as documented-but-not-fixturable and explicitly forbids a synthetic-Registry-extension fixture); the two new orchestration rules by AC-006/TEST-006, AC-043/TEST-043 and AC-052/TEST-052; the A4/A2 addendum gaps by explicit non-action plus a named report path; the transaction/TOCTOU complexity by AC-038..AC-041 and AC-047..AC-049; and the anchor-fingerprint maintenance burden by AC-053/TEST-053's recorded sha256 and ordinal with a relocation regression fixture. Not skipped: high-risk claims are present and each has a surface. One residual noted but not failed here, since it is already the substance of the AC-OBSERVABLE finding: the amendment's own safety claim at :396 ('the Block is fail-closed, no live artifact is created or destroyed') has no test row owning it.
